clay_program:
Clay is a local command-line program for running automations described as JSON workflows. A workflow lists ordered names in `workflow.steps`; `actionSets` maps those names to actions. Each action has a `type`, and normally an `id` that names its output. Later actions receive selected outputs through `includedData` and can insert them into strings with `{name}` placeholders. `when` and `whenNot` provide conditional gates. A `loop` action repeats a child workflow, and `continueKey` selects the child output that decides whether it continues.

Clay supports deterministic automation and model-assisted agents. Available actions can prompt a human, call an OpenAI-compatible model with `scramda2`, read or write approved workspace files, run commands, call APIs, search or browse the web, store memory, and connect workflows to Telegram. The JSON workflow remains the harness: it decides which capabilities run and in what order.

Clay uses an OpenAI-compatible model server. The default endpoint is `http://127.0.0.1:8080`; `GOPHER_URL` can override it. `clay configure` (also `clay config`) configures the server and named model profiles.

Useful CLI commands include `clay workflows` to list workflows, `clay lint <workflow>` to validate one, and `clay dryrun <workflow>` to inspect execution without a normal run. Use `clay --help` and `clay <command> --help` for the installed command syntax.

Clay can run from a terminal, daemon, desktop UI, or Telegram. File reads, file writes, and shell commands have independent approval gates. Clay has no telemetry, account, or vendor service between the user and their configured model server. It is source-available for private, internal, non-commercial use; commercial use requires a separate written license.

The main documentation is README.md for setup and concepts, WORKFLOWS.md for workflow authoring, docs/documentation/02-workflow-schema.md for the schema, and docs/actions/ for individual action types.
